This is the third release candidate of v0.7.0. The epoch-1 engine is gone from every live surface: `eawf init` bears a tree native at epoch 2, and no verb, daemon loop, rule, agent page or test reads or teaches the phase, iter and wave model any more, leaving only the migration and upgrade path to read v1 state. The Claude Code hooks load and report on a native tree; operators can edit, cancel, purge and rename Milestones and Tracks, list and show every entity, title a Task, join a workspace aft

- **A tree is born native.** `eawf init` writes only the skeleton (`config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and builds the epoch-2 generation from the project code; no `.ea/state.json` is written or read. A plain init over an epoch-1 repository still refuses, so its v1 records are never stranded.

- **A created Milestone takes its first plan.** A plan that is not a re-plan now fills a Milestone made by `eawf milestone create` in place when it is PLANNED, native, holds no Batches and no applied plan placed it; before, apply refused its key with `plan_keys_unclaimed`.

- **Milestone and Track maintenance verbs.** `eawf milestone edit` rewrites a PLANNED Milestone's contract; `eawf milestone cancel` also cancels its PLANNED and ACTIVE Batches and their open Tasks and drops its due backlog Tasks in the same commit; `eawf milestone purge` removes a CANCELLED Milestone that no pushed commit carries, with its cancelled and dropped rows; `eawf track rename` retitles an ACTIVE Track and `eawf track set-policy` sets how many ACTIVE Milestones it advises at most.

- **List and show every entity without a daemon.** The `task`, `milestone`, `plan` and `action` groups gain `list` and `show <KEY>`, and a new `decision` group carries the same two reads. They read the selected generation (or the native decision ledger) directly and never open `.ea/state.json`; `eawf task list` filters by `--status` and `--milestone`, and the global flag (`eawf --json task list`) prints JSON.

- **A Task has a title, description, role and effort.** Each is optional and left out of a stored row while unset, so stored rows and approved plan digests stay byte-stable; a title holds at most 80 characters. `eawf task create <URN> --from-spec <FILE>` takes `--title` and `--description` and refuses a value that disagrees with the document; plan apply copies the labels a plan sets, and an untitled Task is shown by its intent up to the first ": ".

- **Join a workspace after init.** `eawf init --workspace <KEY>` joins a registered workspace at birth and refuses an unregistered key before the tree is born; `eawf workspace rekey-repo --to <KEY>` moves a repository out of its own single-member workspace into another, and `eawf workspace remove <KEY>` drops a workspace with exactly one member.

- **Keep heavy scratch out of `.ea/local`.** `eawf local gc` (with `--dry-run`) removes only `.ea/local` entries whose `.retention` date has passed and never follows a link out of the store; the `local_size` doctor check warns past `local.size_warn_mb` (default 1024) and names `local.scratch_root`, where the spike rule now sends virtual environments, models and installs. `worktrees.remove_when_clean` is now read by lease release, and `false` keeps a clean worktree and its branch.

- **Reflect reports every finished Run with its spend.** `eawf reflect run` writes report schema 2: per-Run cost and tokens, totals per project with unpriced Runs counted apart, typed issues and an excluded section; earlier `/reflect` sessions leave the baseline. It takes `--window <N>d`, `--scope project|milestone:<KEY>|track:<KEY>` and `--format text|json`, lists Runs already compacted into the run ledger, and with `--out` writes its fill manifest beside the named report.

- **`eawf validate` checks an epoch-2 generation document** instead of failing it against the epoch-1 model: every native collection that has a document model is checked row by row, each row against the key it is filed under, imported rows against their import shape, and each Batch and Task against the record it is filed under. A copied document without its ledgers warns about unresolved references instead of failing.

- **`eawf bench dispatch <RUN>` scores a dispatched Run's efficiency:** turns (one per API call), read truncation and identical re-read rates, total and cache-read tokens, time to the first succeeded patch and wall clock, against the `fixture` or `real` tier; `--check` exits 2 on a breach, and `--extract` and `--write-extract` read and write a scrubbed extract.

- **Certification per operating system class.** A runtime claim names its `os_classes` (default linux and macos), and each class without its own certification reports `os_class_uncertified`; the provider row also needs a passing live dispatch smoke receipt for each claimed runtime on each claimed class, failing with `dispatch_smoke_missing` or `dispatch_smoke_failed` until it has one.

- **Leaner worker reads.** A Task prompt carries a "Where to start" section naming the write claims and each criterion's proof locus and asks for independent reads in one turn; `repo_read` returns the whole window up to `byte_cap` at whole lines instead of cutting it at 200 lines, and a repeated window is answered by reference with `same_as_call` unless the call sets `reread: true`.

- **Cache reads are metered at their price.** The in-flight governor's `cache_read_weight` (default 0.1, between 0 and 1) weights cache-read tokens against a Run's token cap, and `eawf config set` now writes a mapping leaf such as `economics.governor` as YAML or JSON, from every durable layer including the local one.
- **Claude 5 models are priced** from Anthropic's published rate page, so Runs on `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` count in cost totals.

- **Console transcript.** One row per tool call, updated in place as the call moves; each finished row shows its call and model turn seconds and a turn's input and output tokens; usage totals end the STATE row; a queued or running Run ends on a greyed row naming its wait; Page Up, Page Down and the mouse wheel move through blocks and landing on the newest block follows the tail again; and the scrollbar draws an accent thumb on a track.

- **Doctor checks.** `canonical_sequence_drift` warns when the committed document's sequence lags the newest committed change in its change feed, and an advisory STE (Simplified Technical English) prose lint and an always-passing `ste-prose` hook check the rule modules, profiles and skill bodies.

- **Reopen an acceptance review.** `eawf milestone reopen-review <URN>` returns a Milestone in acceptance review to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so it can take an appended Batch; the next `eawf milestone open-review` files a successor acceptance bundle, and an approval sealed on the earlier bundle can no longer accept the Milestone.

- **Reopen an accepted Milestone.** `eawf milestone reopen <URN>` returns a COMPLETED Milestone to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so a fix can land in it before it ships. Only an operator principal may reopen it, and a Milestone that a release record or a pushed release tag names is refused. The acceptance stays in the ledger as history, and the approval it was accepted on can never accept it again.

- **`eawf release canary-export <version> --os-class <class>`** writes a release's native canary evidence export from the certifications `eawf runtime certify` now stores in full, copying each stored record unchanged and refusing a claimed class no stored certification covers.

- **Claude Code certifies on Linux.** Its project document has no byte cap (the model's context window governs), measured on claude-code 2.1.310 and recorded as a certified uncapped fact, so the certify stage no longer refuses with `runtime_facts_uncertified`.

- **`eawf store redact-content` takes a leak out before it is committed.** It compares the artifact ledger with its bytes in HEAD and withholds each line the leak scan now flags in the content rows filed since, keeping each row's reference; committed rows stay as they are.

- **The epoch-1 engine is removed from every live surface.** `eawf status` reads only the native generation and reports the primary Track, active Milestone, open Tasks and native decisions; the daemon no longer schedules its stale-wave and session time-to-live sweeps; the v1 state readers are ported to the generation or retired, among them the epoch-1 `why` targets and the v1-only doctor checks; and the close-gate and spec-jury chain and other code with no production caller is deleted, with lint

- **Retired verbs.** `eawf jury label` exits 2 with `LegacyOperationRemoved` naming `eawf batch label`, and `eawf jury` is an unknown command; `eawf impact` is retired; `eawf release pipeline` takes `--milestone` as its only, required subject, so `--phase` is a usage error, and the phase-release workflow is gone.

- **The Claude Code plugin hooks load and report on a native tree.** The hook manifest is written to `hooks/hooks.json`, where Claude Code reads it, the session-end hook subscribes to SessionEnd instead of Stop, which fires every turn, and the agent_end and agent-output hooks resolve role and scope from the native Run instead of v1 state.

- **The shipped rules, profiles, role pages, help topics and skill bodies teach the native model** of Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and PlanRevision; the docs census and a source census hold every epoch-1 word left in `src/` outside migration and upgrade paths to a reasoned allowlist row, and no such file may spell an epoch-1 id.

- **The bundled `state.schema.json` describes the generation document,** with one object of rows per collection, instead of the v1 State model; `plan-view.schema.json` and the plan view renderer are deleted, as are the unraised error codes `WAVE_DEPS_NOT_SATISFIED`, `PHASE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ITER_NOT_ACTIVE` and `WAVE_OUT_OF_ORDER_REJECTED`.

- **The commit gates keep only the native grammar.** The wave, bare phase and `Eawf-Wave` commit forms, the open-phase rule and the release annotation check are gone, with the `wave-trailer-guard`, `spec-paths` and `eawf016-title-clarity` hooks; history written in the old subject forms still passes `--check-history`.

- **Imported backlog rows can leave the backlog.** `eawf task drop` on an epoch-1 key the cutover imported files the row as DROPPED without rewriting the sealed snapshot; a second drop is refused with `legacy_edge_refused`.

- **A committed ledger append advances the committed sequence,** so callers reading it are no longer refused with a revision conflict, and `eawf publish` stages a first, unstaged path whole instead of leaving `state.json` dirty and refusing the next publish with `publish_dirty_tree`.
- **Claude usage is folded at each message's latest reading,** so output tokens are no longer undercounted for the budget meter and the scorecard.
- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

- **Render lock files are bounded.** Render targets map onto 256 fixed stripe lock files instead of one file per target path, and the daemon test harnesses remove each whole runtime directory on teardown.
- **`eawf doctor` warns instead of crashing on a malformed config layer;** the local-size check degrades to a warning naming the merge failure.

- **Repository settings load in current Claude Code.** The managed metadata block in `.claude/settings.json` now names its hook list `hook_scripts`: Claude Code 2.1.310 refused the whole file while that block carried its own `hooks` key, which dropped every eawf hook, the status line and the env settings of a repository install. `eawf plugin update claude` rewrites an rc2 install.

- **A reopened review cannot reuse an earlier seal.** `eawf milestone open-review` now requires the acceptance bundle revision after the newest filed bundle, or revision 1 when none is filed. Before, a review reopened and opened again on revision 1 let an approval sealed in the earlier review accept the Milestone. The console no longer suggests `eawf milestone accept`, or an earlier review's waiting question, for a reopened Milestone.

- **A freshly initialised tree has its project row,** so memory, MCP, dispatch-control and `record append` writes work right after `eawf init`; `eawf why` explains decisions imported from the old model, and init reports the generation document as its state path.

- **`eawf plugin doctor claude` flags an rc2 install** whose settings Claude Code refuses or whose `Stop` hook no longer runs, and reports hooks loaded twice beside the marketplace plugin, each with its fix; agent pages no longer carry a `memory` key Claude Code rejects.

- **Safer maintenance.** Cancelling a Milestone asks a running Task's live Run to cancel, `eawf milestone purge` refuses while another record names the purged work, a retried legacy `task drop` replays its receipt, and `eawf local gc` keeps an expired entry that holds an unexpired one.

- **Leaner Run receipts and honest totals.** A `repo_read` receipt is stored by digest instead of text, a repeat read matches only the same file and launch, dispatch scoring counts each API call once, and `eawf reflect` counts as unpriced only Runs that reported tokens without a cost.

- **Upgrades keep work moving.** A governor written before `cache_read_weight` keeps its digest, so a Run admitted under rc2 resumes, and a gate stored with a legacy cadence keeps its digest, so its receipts stay fresh.
- **The release re-typed-rule census counts only operator-typed prose,** not the prompts an orchestrating agent sends its subagents.

- **Server checkout and runtime paths no longer reach committed state.** The leak scan treats a path under `/srv`, a `/run/user/<uid>` runtime directory and a `pytest-of-<user>` temp root like a home directory, so captured Run output withholds the line, a state write carrying one is refused and `path-leak-lint` flags it; the epoch-1 cutover scan keeps its three home anchors.

- **Agent report bodies use native field names.** `wave_id`, `waves`, `phase_id` and `completed_wave_ids` are now `task_key`, `tasks`, `milestone_key` and `completed_task_keys`; a new body naming an old field is refused with `extra_forbidden`, while a stored row is upgraded once on read and never rewritten.

- **Audit and gate cadences name native scopes.** `every-wave` becomes `every-task`, `every-iter` becomes `every-batch` and `every-phase` becomes `every-milestone`; `ship` and `manual` stay. A stored gate row reads an old value as its native one, an authored profile check or audit document naming one is refused with the value to write, and the `eawf doctor --fix` config normalisation rewrites each layer once.

- **Rule and profile block ids are renamed** where they spelled an epoch-1 noun, among them `wave-verification-scope` to `task-verification-scope`, `repo.phase-equals-release` to `repo.milestone-equals-release` and `repo.large-phase-pr` to `repo.large-milestone-pr`; re-render with `eawf sync`, and re-render installed hooks with `eawf plugin update claude`.

- **Retired settings.** `planning.max_parallel_waves`, `verify.require_iter_audit_accepted`, `daemon.session_handle_ttl_seconds`, `dispatch.role_tier_token_cap` and `profiles.certified` have no reader left and are deprecated. `eawf doctor` names each one a layer still states; remove it with `eawf config unset <key>` (add `--scope local|global|workspace` for another layer) or `eawf doctor --fix`.

- **`eawf workspace rekey-repo` moves registry rows only;** it does not rewrite store rows whose URNs carry the old workspace key, and neither new workspace verb is served by a daemon remote procedure call (RPC) yet.

- **Not in this release:** a multi-project aggregate console route, `eawf reflect` cohorts, estimate-versus-actual variance and workspace-wide reflect scopes are planned for 0.7.1, and prose is not yet rewritten to STE; only the advisory lint ships.

+This is the third release candidate of v0.7.0. The epoch-1 engine is gone from every live surface: `eawf init` bears a tree native at epoch 2, and no verb, daemon loop, rule, agent page or test reads or teaches the phase, iter and wave model any more, leaving only the migration and upgrade path to read v1 state. The Claude Code hooks load and report on a native tree; operators can edit, cancel, purge and rename Milestones and Tracks, list and show every entity, title a Task, join a workspace af

+- **A tree is born native.** `eawf init` writes only the skeleton (`config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and builds the epoch-2 generation from the project code; no `.ea/state.json` is written or read. A plain init over an epoch-1 repository still refuses, so its v1 records are never stranded.

+- **A created Milestone takes its first plan.** A plan that is not a re-plan now fills a Milestone made by `eawf milestone create` in place when it is PLANNED, native, holds no Batches and no applied plan placed it; before, apply refused its key with `plan_keys_unclaimed`.

+- **Milestone and Track maintenance verbs.** `eawf milestone edit` rewrites a PLANNED Milestone's contract; `eawf milestone cancel` also cancels its PLANNED and ACTIVE Batches and their open Tasks and drops its due backlog Tasks in the same commit; `eawf milestone purge` removes a CANCELLED Milestone that no pushed commit carries, with its cancelled and dropped rows; `eawf track rename` retitles an ACTIVE Track and `eawf track set-policy` sets how many ACTIVE Milestones it advises at most.

+- **List and show every entity without a daemon.** The `task`, `milestone`, `plan` and `action` groups gain `list` and `show <KEY>`, and a new `decision` group carries the same two reads. They read the selected generation (or the native decision ledger) directly and never open `.ea/state.json`; `eawf task list` filters by `--status` and `--milestone`, and the global flag (`eawf --json task list`) prints JSON.

+- **A Task has a title, description, role and effort.** Each is optional and left out of a stored row while unset, so stored rows and approved plan digests stay byte-stable; a title holds at most 80 characters. `eawf task create <URN> --from-spec <FILE>` takes `--title` and `--description` and refuses a value that disagrees with the document; plan apply copies the labels a plan sets, and an untitled Task is shown by its intent up to the first ": ".

+- **Join a workspace after init.** `eawf init --workspace <KEY>` joins a registered workspace at birth and refuses an unregistered key before the tree is born; `eawf workspace rekey-repo --to <KEY>` moves a repository out of its own single-member workspace into another, and `eawf workspace remove <KEY>` drops a workspace with exactly one member.

+- **Keep heavy scratch out of `.ea/local`.** `eawf local gc` (with `--dry-run`) removes only `.ea/local` entries whose `.retention` date has passed and never follows a link out of the store; the `local_size` doctor check warns past `local.size_warn_mb` (default 1024) and names `local.scratch_root`, where the spike rule now sends virtual environments, models and installs. `worktrees.remove_when_clean` is now read by lease release, and `false` keeps a clean worktree and its branch.

+- **Reflect reports every finished Run with its spend.** `eawf reflect run` writes report schema 2: per-Run cost and tokens, totals per project with unpriced Runs counted apart, typed issues and an excluded section; earlier `/reflect` sessions leave the baseline. It takes `--window <N>d`, `--scope project|milestone:<KEY>|track:<KEY>` and `--format text|json`, lists Runs already compacted into the run ledger, and with `--out` writes its fill manifest beside the named report.

+- **`eawf validate` checks an epoch-2 generation document,** each native row against its own model and each Batch and Task against the record it is filed under, instead of failing it against the epoch-1 model.

+- **`eawf bench dispatch <RUN>` scores a dispatched Run's efficiency:** turns, read truncation and identical re-read rates, billable and cache-read tokens, time to the first succeeded patch and wall clock, against the `fixture` or `real` tier; `--check` exits 2 on a breach, and `--extract` and `--write-extract` read and write a scrubbed extract.

+- **Certification per operating system class.** A runtime claim names its `os_classes` (default linux and macos), and each class without its own certification reports `os_class_uncertified`; the provider row also needs a passing live dispatch smoke receipt per claimed class, failing with `dispatch_smoke_missing` or `dispatch_smoke_failed` until it has one.

+- **Leaner worker reads.** A Task prompt carries a "Where to start" section naming the write claims and each criterion's proof locus and asks for independent reads in one turn; `repo_read` returns the whole window up to `byte_cap` at whole lines instead of cutting it at 200 lines, and a repeated window is answered by reference with `same_as_call` unless the call sets `reread: true`.

+- **Cache reads are metered at their price.** The in-flight governor's `cache_read_weight` (default 0.1, between 0 and 1) weights cache-read tokens against a Run's token cap, and `eawf config set` now writes a mapping leaf such as `economics.governor` as YAML or JSON, from every durable layer including the local one.
+- **Claude 5 models are priced** from Anthropic's published rate page, so Runs on `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` count in cost totals.

+- **Console transcript.** One row per tool call, updated in place as the call moves; each finished row shows its call and model turn seconds and a turn's input and output tokens; usage totals end the STATE row; a queued or running Run ends on a greyed row naming its wait; Page Up, Page Down and the mouse wheel move through blocks and landing on the newest block follows the tail again; and the scrollbar draws an accent thumb on a track.

+- **Doctor checks.** `canonical_sequence_drift` warns when the committed sequence lags the daemon's live one, and an advisory STE (Simplified Technical English) prose lint and an always-passing `ste-prose` hook check the rule modules, profiles and skill bodies.

+- **The epoch-1 engine is removed from every live surface.** `eawf status` reads only the native generation and reports the primary Track, active Milestone, open Tasks and native decisions; the daemon no longer schedules its stale-wave and session time-to-live sweeps; the v1 state readers are ported to the generation or retired, among them the epoch-1 `why` targets and the v1-only doctor checks; and the close-gate and spec-jury chain and other code with no production caller is deleted, with lin

+- **Retired verbs.** `eawf jury label` exits 2 with `LegacyOperationRemoved` naming `eawf batch label`, and `eawf jury` is an unknown command; `eawf impact` is retired; `eawf release pipeline` takes `--milestone` as its only, required subject, so `--phase` is a usage error, and the phase-release workflow is gone.

+- **The Claude Code plugin hooks load and report on a native tree.** The hook manifest is written to `hooks/hooks.json`, where Claude Code reads it, the session-end hook subscribes to SessionEnd instead of Stop, which fires every turn, and the agent_end and agent-output hooks resolve role and scope from the native Run instead of v1 state.

+- **The shipped rules, profiles, role pages, help topics and skill bodies teach the native model** of Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and PlanRevision; the docs census and a source census hold every epoch-1 word left in `src/` outside migration and upgrade paths to a reasoned allowlist row, and no such file may spell an epoch-1 id.

+- **The bundled `state.schema.json` describes the generation document,** with one object of rows per collection, instead of the v1 State model; `plan-view.schema.json` and the plan view renderer are deleted, as are the unraised error codes `WAVE_DEPS_NOT_SATISFIED`, `PHASE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ITER_NOT_ACTIVE` and `WAVE_OUT_OF_ORDER_REJECTED`.

+- **The commit gates keep only the native grammar.** The wave, bare phase and `Eawf-Wave` commit forms, the open-phase rule and the release annotation check are gone, with the `wave-trailer-guard`, `spec-paths` and `eawf016-title-clarity` hooks; history written in the old subject forms still passes `--check-history`.

+- **Imported backlog rows can leave the backlog.** `eawf task drop` on an epoch-1 key the cutover imported files the row as DROPPED without rewriting the sealed snapshot; a second drop is refused with `legacy_edge_refused`.

+- **A committed ledger append advances the committed sequence,** so callers reading it are no longer refused with a revision conflict, and `eawf publish` stages a first, unstaged path whole instead of leaving `state.json` dirty and refusing the next publish with `publish_dirty_tree`.
+- **Claude usage is folded at each message's latest reading,** so output tokens are no longer undercounted for the budget meter and the scorecard.
+- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

+- **Render lock files are bounded.** Render targets map onto 256 fixed stripe lock files instead of one file per target path, and the daemon test harnesses remove each whole runtime directory on teardown.
+- **`eawf doctor` warns instead of crashing on a malformed config layer;** the local-size check degrades to a warning naming the merge failure.

+- **Agent report bodies use native field names.** `wave_id`, `waves`, `phase_id` and `completed_wave_ids` are now `task_key`, `tasks`, `milestone_key` and `completed_task_keys`; a new body naming an old field is refused with `extra_forbidden`, while a stored row is upgraded once on read and never rewritten.

+- **Audit and gate cadences name native scopes.** `every-wave` becomes `every-task`, `every-iter` becomes `every-batch` and `every-phase` becomes `every-milestone`; `ship` and `manual` stay. A stored gate row reads an old value as its native one, an authored profile check or audit document naming one is refused with the value to write, and the `eawf doctor --fix` config normalisation rewrites each layer once.

+- **Rule and profile block ids are renamed** where they spelled an epoch-1 noun, among them `wave-verification-scope` to `task-verification-scope`, `repo.phase-equals-release` to `repo.milestone-equals-release` and `repo.large-phase-pr` to `repo.large-milestone-pr`; re-render with `eawf sync`, and re-render installed hooks with `eawf plugin update claude`.

+- **Retired settings.** `planning.max_parallel_waves`, `verify.require_iter_audit_accepted` and `daemon.session_handle_ttl_seconds` have no reader left and are deprecated; remove them from your layers with `eawf config unset`.

+- **`eawf workspace rekey-repo` moves registry rows only;** it does not rewrite store rows whose URNs carry the old workspace key, and neither new workspace verb is served by a daemon remote procedure call (RPC) yet.

+- **Not in this release:** a multi-project aggregate console route, `eawf reflect` cohorts, estimate-versus-actual variance and workspace-wide reflect scopes are planned for 0.7.1, and prose is not yet rewritten to STE; only the advisory lint ships.

9-This is the third release candidate of v0.7.0. The epoch-1 engine is gone from every live surface: `eawf init` bears a tree native at epoch 2, and no verb, daemon loop, rule, agent page or test reads or teaches the phase, iter and wave model any more, leaving only the migration and upgrade path to read v1 state. The Claude Code hooks load and report on a native tree; operators can edit, cancel, purge and rename Milestones and Tracks, list and show every entity, title a Task, join a workspace a

13-- **A tree is born native.** `eawf init` writes only the skeleton (`config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and builds the epoch-2 generation from the project code; no `.ea/state.json` is written or read. A plain init over an epoch-1 repository still refuses, so its v1 records are never stranded.

14-- **A created Milestone takes its first plan.** A plan that is not a re-plan now fills a Milestone made by `eawf milestone create` in place when it is PLANNED, native, holds no Batches and no applied plan placed it; before, apply refused its key with `plan_keys_unclaimed`.

15-- **Milestone and Track maintenance verbs.** `eawf milestone edit` rewrites a PLANNED Milestone's contract; `eawf milestone cancel` also cancels its PLANNED and ACTIVE Batches and their open Tasks and drops its due backlog Tasks in the same commit; `eawf milestone purge` removes a CANCELLED Milestone that no pushed commit carries, with its cancelled and dropped rows; `eawf track rename` retitles an ACTIVE Track and `eawf track set-policy` sets how many ACTIVE Milestones it advises at most.

16-- **List and show every entity without a daemon.** The `task`, `milestone`, `plan` and `action` groups gain `list` and `show <KEY>`, and a new `decision` group carries the same two reads. They read the selected generation (or the native decision ledger) directly and never open `.ea/state.json`; `eawf task list` filters by `--status` and `--milestone`, and the global flag (`eawf --json task list`) prints JSON.

17-- **A Task has a title, description, role and effort.** Each is optional and left out of a stored row while unset, so stored rows and approved plan digests stay byte-stable; a title holds at most 80 characters. `eawf task create <URN> --from-spec <FILE>` takes `--title` and `--description` and refuses a value that disagrees with the document; plan apply copies the labels a plan sets, and an untitled Task is shown by its intent up to the first ": ".

18-- **Join a workspace after init.** `eawf init --workspace <KEY>` joins a registered workspace at birth and refuses an unregistered key before the tree is born; `eawf workspace rekey-repo --to <KEY>` moves a repository out of its own single-member workspace into another, and `eawf workspace remove <KEY>` drops a workspace with exactly one member.

19-- **Keep heavy scratch out of `.ea/local`.** `eawf local gc` (with `--dry-run`) removes only `.ea/local` entries whose `.retention` date has passed and never follows a link out of the store; the `local_size` doctor check warns past `local.size_warn_mb` (default 1024) and names `local.scratch_root`, where the spike rule now sends virtual environments, models and installs. `worktrees.remove_when_clean` is now read by lease release, and `false` keeps a clean worktree and its branch.

20-- **Reflect reports every finished Run with its spend.** `eawf reflect run` writes report schema 2: per-Run cost and tokens, totals per project with unpriced Runs counted apart, typed issues and an excluded section; earlier `/reflect` sessions leave the baseline. It takes `--window <N>d`, `--scope project|milestone:<KEY>|track:<KEY>` and `--format text|json`, lists Runs already compacted into the run ledger, and with `--out` writes its fill manifest beside the named report.

21-- **`eawf validate` checks an epoch-2 generation document** instead of failing it against the epoch-1 model: every native collection that has a document model is checked row by row, each row against the key it is filed under, imported rows against their import shape, and each Batch and Task against the record it is filed under. A copied document without its ledgers warns about unresolved references instead of failing.

22-- **`eawf bench dispatch <RUN>` scores a dispatched Run's efficiency:** turns (one per API call), read truncation and identical re-read rates, total and cache-read tokens, time to the first succeeded patch and wall clock, against the `fixture` or `real` tier; `--check` exits 2 on a breach, and `--extract` and `--write-extract` read and write a scrubbed extract.

23-- **Certification per operating system class.** A runtime claim names its `os_classes` (default linux and macos), and each class without its own certification reports `os_class_uncertified`; the provider row also needs a passing live dispatch smoke receipt for each claimed runtime on each claimed class, failing with `dispatch_smoke_missing` or `dispatch_smoke_failed` until it has one.

24-- **Leaner worker reads.** A Task prompt carries a "Where to start" section naming the write claims and each criterion's proof locus and asks for independent reads in one turn; `repo_read` returns the whole window up to `byte_cap` at whole lines instead of cutting it at 200 lines, and a repeated window is answered by reference with `same_as_call` unless the call sets `reread: true`.

25-- **Cache reads are metered at their price.** The in-flight governor's `cache_read_weight` (default 0.1, between 0 and 1) weights cache-read tokens against a Run's token cap, and `eawf config set` now writes a mapping leaf such as `economics.governor` as YAML or JSON, from every durable layer including the local one.
26-- **Claude 5 models are priced** from Anthropic's published rate page, so Runs on `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` count in cost totals.

27-- **Console transcript.** One row per tool call, updated in place as the call moves; each finished row shows its call and model turn seconds and a turn's input and output tokens; usage totals end the STATE row; a queued or running Run ends on a greyed row naming its wait; Page Up, Page Down and the mouse wheel move through blocks and landing on the newest block follows the tail again; and the scrollbar draws an accent thumb on a track.

28-- **Doctor checks.** `canonical_sequence_drift` warns when the committed document's sequence lags the newest committed change in its change feed, and an advisory STE (Simplified Technical English) prose lint and an always-passing `ste-prose` hook check the rule modules, profiles and skill bodies.

29-- **Reopen an acceptance review.** `eawf milestone reopen-review <URN>` returns a Milestone in acceptance review to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so it can take an appended Batch; the next `eawf milestone open-review` files a successor acceptance bundle, and an approval sealed on the earlier bundle can no longer accept the Milestone.

30-- **Reopen an accepted Milestone.** `eawf milestone reopen <URN>` returns a COMPLETED Milestone to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so a fix can land in it before it ships. Only an operator principal may reopen it, and a Milestone that a release record or a pushed release tag names is refused. The acceptance stays in the ledger as history, and the approval it was accepted on can never accept it again.

31-- **`eawf release canary-export <version> --os-class <class>`** writes a release's native canary evidence export from the certifications `eawf runtime certify` now stores in full, copying each stored record unchanged and refusing a claimed class no stored certification covers.

32-- **Claude Code certifies on Linux.** Its project document has no byte cap (the model's context window governs), measured on claude-code 2.1.310 and recorded as a certified uncapped fact, so the certify stage no longer refuses with `runtime_facts_uncertified`.

33-- **`eawf store redact-content` takes a leak out before it is committed.** It compares the artifact ledger with its bytes in HEAD and withholds each line the leak scan now flags in the content rows filed since, keeping each row's reference; committed rows stay as they are.

37-- **The epoch-1 engine is removed from every live surface.** `eawf status` reads only the native generation and reports the primary Track, active Milestone, open Tasks and native decisions; the daemon no longer schedules its stale-wave and session time-to-live sweeps; the v1 state readers are ported to the generation or retired, among them the epoch-1 `why` targets and the v1-only doctor checks; and the close-gate and spec-jury chain and other code with no production caller is deleted, with l

38-- **Retired verbs.** `eawf jury label` exits 2 with `LegacyOperationRemoved` naming `eawf batch label`, and `eawf jury` is an unknown command; `eawf impact` is retired; `eawf release pipeline` takes `--milestone` as its only, required subject, so `--phase` is a usage error, and the phase-release workflow is gone.

39-- **The Claude Code plugin hooks load and report on a native tree.** The hook manifest is written to `hooks/hooks.json`, where Claude Code reads it, the session-end hook subscribes to SessionEnd instead of Stop, which fires every turn, and the agent_end and agent-output hooks resolve role and scope from the native Run instead of v1 state.

40-- **The shipped rules, profiles, role pages, help topics and skill bodies teach the native model** of Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and PlanRevision; the docs census and a source census hold every epoch-1 word left in `src/` outside migration and upgrade paths to a reasoned allowlist row, and no such file may spell an epoch-1 id.

41-- **The bundled `state.schema.json` describes the generation document,** with one object of rows per collection, instead of the v1 State model; `plan-view.schema.json` and the plan view renderer are deleted, as are the unraised error codes `WAVE_DEPS_NOT_SATISFIED`, `PHASE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ITER_NOT_ACTIVE` and `WAVE_OUT_OF_ORDER_REJECTED`.

42-- **The commit gates keep only the native grammar.** The wave, bare phase and `Eawf-Wave` commit forms, the open-phase rule and the release annotation check are gone, with the `wave-trailer-guard`, `spec-paths` and `eawf016-title-clarity` hooks; history written in the old subject forms still passes `--check-history`.

43-- **Imported backlog rows can leave the backlog.** `eawf task drop` on an epoch-1 key the cutover imported files the row as DROPPED without rewriting the sealed snapshot; a second drop is refused with `legacy_edge_refused`.

44-- **A committed ledger append advances the committed sequence,** so callers reading it are no longer refused with a revision conflict, and `eawf publish` stages a first, unstaged path whole instead of leaving `state.json` dirty and refusing the next publish with `publish_dirty_tree`.
45-- **Claude usage is folded at each message's latest reading,** so output tokens are no longer undercounted for the budget meter and the scorecard.
46-- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

47-- **Render lock files are bounded.** Render targets map onto 256 fixed stripe lock files instead of one file per target path, and the daemon test harnesses remove each whole runtime directory on teardown.
48-- **`eawf doctor` warns instead of crashing on a malformed config layer;** the local-size check degrades to a warning naming the merge failure.

49-- **Repository settings load in current Claude Code.** The managed metadata block in `.claude/settings.json` now names its hook list `hook_scripts`: Claude Code 2.1.310 refused the whole file while that block carried its own `hooks` key, which dropped every eawf hook, the status line and the env settings of a repository install. `eawf plugin update claude` rewrites an rc2 install.

50-- **A reopened review cannot reuse an earlier seal.** `eawf milestone open-review` now requires the acceptance bundle revision after the newest filed bundle, or revision 1 when none is filed. Before, a review reopened and opened again on revision 1 let an approval sealed in the earlier review accept the Milestone. The console no longer suggests `eawf milestone accept`, or an earlier review's waiting question, for a reopened Milestone.

51-- **A freshly initialised tree has its project row,** so memory, MCP, dispatch-control and `record append` writes work right after `eawf init`; `eawf why` explains decisions imported from the old model, and init reports the generation document as its state path.

52-- **`eawf plugin doctor claude` flags an rc2 install** whose settings Claude Code refuses or whose `Stop` hook no longer runs, and reports hooks loaded twice beside the marketplace plugin, each with its fix; agent pages no longer carry a `memory` key Claude Code rejects.

53-- **Safer maintenance.** Cancelling a Milestone asks a running Task's live Run to cancel, `eawf milestone purge` refuses while another record names the purged work, a retried legacy `task drop` replays its receipt, and `eawf local gc` keeps an expired entry that holds an unexpired one.

54-- **Leaner Run receipts and honest totals.** A `repo_read` receipt is stored by digest instead of text, a repeat read matches only the same file and launch, dispatch scoring counts each API call once, and `eawf reflect` counts as unpriced only Runs that reported tokens without a cost.

55-- **Upgrades keep work moving.** A governor written before `cache_read_weight` keeps its digest, so a Run admitted under rc2 resumes, and a gate stored with a legacy cadence keeps its digest, so its receipts stay fresh.
56-- **The release re-typed-rule census counts only operator-typed prose,** not the prompts an orchestrating agent sends its subagents.

57-- **Server checkout and runtime paths no longer reach committed state.** The leak scan treats a path under `/srv`, a `/run/user/<uid>` runtime directory and a `pytest-of-<user>` temp root like a home directory, so captured Run output withholds the line, a state write carrying one is refused and `path-leak-lint` flags it; the epoch-1 cutover scan keeps its three home anchors.

61-- **Agent report bodies use native field names.** `wave_id`, `waves`, `phase_id` and `completed_wave_ids` are now `task_key`, `tasks`, `milestone_key` and `completed_task_keys`; a new body naming an old field is refused with `extra_forbidden`, while a stored row is upgraded once on read and never rewritten.

62-- **Audit and gate cadences name native scopes.** `every-wave` becomes `every-task`, `every-iter` becomes `every-batch` and `every-phase` becomes `every-milestone`; `ship` and `manual` stay. A stored gate row reads an old value as its native one, an authored profile check or audit document naming one is refused with the value to write, and the `eawf doctor --fix` config normalisation rewrites each layer once.

63-- **Rule and profile block ids are renamed** where they spelled an epoch-1 noun, among them `wave-verification-scope` to `task-verification-scope`, `repo.phase-equals-release` to `repo.milestone-equals-release` and `repo.large-phase-pr` to `repo.large-milestone-pr`; re-render with `eawf sync`, and re-render installed hooks with `eawf plugin update claude`.

3	This is the third release candidate of v0.7.0. The epoch-1 engine is gone from every live surface: `eawf init` bears a tree native at epoch 2, and no verb, daemon loop, rule, agent page or test reads or teaches the phase, iter and wave model any more, leaving only the migration and upgrade path to read v1 state. The Claude Code hooks load and report on a native tree; operators can edit, cancel, purge and rename Milestones and Tracks, list and show every entity, title a Task, join a worksp

7	- **A tree is born native.** `eawf init` writes only the skeleton (`config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and builds the epoch-2 generation from the project code; no `.ea/state.json` is written or read. A plain init over an epoch-1 repository still refuses, so its v1 records are never stranded.

8	- **A created Milestone takes its first plan.** A plan that is not a re-plan now fills a Milestone made by `eawf milestone create` in place when it is PLANNED, native, holds no Batches and no applied plan placed it; before, apply refused its key with `plan_keys_unclaimed`.

9	- **Milestone and Track maintenance verbs.** `eawf milestone edit` rewrites a PLANNED Milestone's contract; `eawf milestone cancel` also cancels its PLANNED and ACTIVE Batches and their open Tasks and drops its due backlog Tasks in the same commit; `eawf milestone purge` removes a CANCELLED Milestone that no pushed commit carries, with its cancelled and dropped rows; `eawf track rename` retitles an ACTIVE Track and `eawf track set-policy` sets how many ACTIVE Milestones it advises at most

10	- **List and show every entity without a daemon.** The `task`, `milestone`, `plan` and `action` groups gain `list` and `show <KEY>`, and a new `decision` group carries the same two reads. They read the selected generation (or the native decision ledger) directly and never open `.ea/state.json`; `eawf task list` filters by `--status` and `--milestone`, and the global flag (`eawf --json task list`) prints JSON.

11	- **A Task has a title, description, role and effort.** Each is optional and left out of a stored row while unset, so stored rows and approved plan digests stay byte-stable; a title holds at most 80 characters. `eawf task create <URN> --from-spec <FILE>` takes `--title` and `--description` and refuses a value that disagrees with the document; plan apply copies the labels a plan sets, and an untitled Task is shown by its intent up to the first ": ".

12	- **Join a workspace after init.** `eawf init --workspace <KEY>` joins a registered workspace at birth and refuses an unregistered key before the tree is born; `eawf workspace rekey-repo --to <KEY>` moves a repository out of its own single-member workspace into another, and `eawf workspace remove <KEY>` drops a workspace with exactly one member.

13	- **Keep heavy scratch out of `.ea/local`.** `eawf local gc` (with `--dry-run`) removes only `.ea/local` entries whose `.retention` date has passed and never follows a link out of the store; the `local_size` doctor check warns past `local.size_warn_mb` (default 1024) and names `local.scratch_root`, where the spike rule now sends virtual environments, models and installs. `worktrees.remove_when_clean` is now read by lease release, and `false` keeps a clean worktree and its branch.

14	- **Reflect reports every finished Run with its spend.** `eawf reflect run` writes report schema 2: per-Run cost and tokens, totals per project with unpriced Runs counted apart, typed issues and an excluded section; earlier `/reflect` sessions leave the baseline. It takes `--window <N>d`, `--scope project|milestone:<KEY>|track:<KEY>` and `--format text|json`, lists Runs already compacted into the run ledger, and with `--out` writes its fill manifest beside the named report.

15	- **`eawf validate` checks an epoch-2 generation document** instead of failing it against the epoch-1 model: every native collection that has a document model is checked row by row, each row against the key it is filed under, imported rows against their import shape, and each Batch and Task against the record it is filed under. A copied document without its ledgers warns about unresolved references instead of failing.

16	- **`eawf bench dispatch <RUN>` scores a dispatched Run's efficiency:** turns (one per API call), read truncation and identical re-read rates, total and cache-read tokens, time to the first succeeded patch and wall clock, against the `fixture` or `real` tier; `--check` exits 2 on a breach, and `--extract` and `--write-extract` read and write a scrubbed extract.

17	- **Certification per operating system class.** A runtime claim names its `os_classes` (default linux and macos), and each class without its own certification reports `os_class_uncertified`; the provider row also needs a passing live dispatch smoke receipt for each claimed runtime on each claimed class, failing with `dispatch_smoke_missing` or `dispatch_smoke_failed` until it has one.

18	- **Leaner worker reads.** A Task prompt carries a "Where to start" section naming the write claims and each criterion's proof locus and asks for independent reads in one turn; `repo_read` returns the whole window up to `byte_cap` at whole lines instead of cutting it at 200 lines, and a repeated window is answered by reference with `same_as_call` unless the call sets `reread: true`.

19	- **Cache reads are metered at their price.** The in-flight governor's `cache_read_weight` (default 0.1, between 0 and 1) weights cache-read tokens against a Run's token cap, and `eawf config set` now writes a mapping leaf such as `economics.governor` as YAML or JSON, from every durable layer including the local one.
20	- **Claude 5 models are priced** from Anthropic's published rate page, so Runs on `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` count in cost totals.

21	- **Console transcript.** One row per tool call, updated in place as the call moves; each finished row shows its call and model turn seconds and a turn's input and output tokens; usage totals end the STATE row; a queued or running Run ends on a greyed row naming its wait; Page Up, Page Down and the mouse wheel move through blocks and landing on the newest block follows the tail again; and the scrollbar draws an accent thumb on a track.

22	- **Doctor checks.** `canonical_sequence_drift` warns when the committed document's sequence lags the newest committed change in its change feed, and an advisory STE (Simplified Technical English) prose lint and an always-passing `ste-prose` hook check the rule modules, profiles and skill bodies.

23	- **Reopen an acceptance review.** `eawf milestone reopen-review <URN>` returns a Milestone in acceptance review to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so it can take an appended Batch; the next `eawf milestone open-review` files a successor acceptance bundle, and an approval sealed on the earlier bundle can no longer accept the Milestone.

24	- **Reopen an accepted Milestone.** `eawf milestone reopen <URN>` returns a COMPLETED Milestone to ACTIVE with a recorded reason, so a fix can land in it before it ships. Only an operator principal may reopen it, and a Milestone that a release record or a pushed release tag names is refused. The acceptance stays in the ledger as history, and the approval it was accepted on can never accept it again.

25	- **`eawf release canary-export <version> --os-class <class>`** writes a release's native canary evidence export from the certifications `eawf runtime certify` now stores in full, copying each stored record unchanged and refusing a claimed class no stored certification covers.

26	- **Claude Code certifies on Linux.** Its project document has no byte cap (the model's context window governs), measured on claude-code 2.1.310 and recorded as a certified uncapped fact, so the certify stage no longer refuses with `runtime_facts_uncertified`.

27	- **`eawf store redact-content` takes a leak out before it is committed.** It compares the artifact ledger with its bytes in HEAD and withholds each line the leak scan now flags in the content rows filed since, keeping each row's reference; committed rows stay as they are.

31	- **The epoch-1 engine is removed from every live surface.** `eawf status` reads only the native generation and reports the primary Track, active Milestone, open Tasks and native decisions; the daemon no longer schedules its stale-wave and session time-to-live sweeps; the v1 state readers are ported to the generation or retired, among them the epoch-1 `why` targets and the v1-only doctor checks; and the close-gate and spec-jury chain and other code with no production caller is deleted, wi

32	- **Retired verbs.** `eawf jury label` exits 2 with `LegacyOperationRemoved` naming `eawf batch label`, and `eawf jury` is an unknown command; `eawf impact` is retired; `eawf release pipeline` takes `--milestone` as its only, required subject, so `--phase` is a usage error, and the phase-release workflow is gone.

33	- **The Claude Code plugin hooks load and report on a native tree.** The hook manifest is written to `hooks/hooks.json`, where Claude Code reads it, the session-end hook subscribes to SessionEnd instead of Stop, which fires every turn, and the agent_end and agent-output hooks resolve role and scope from the native Run instead of v1 state.

34	- **The shipped rules, profiles, role pages, help topics and skill bodies teach the native model** of Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and PlanRevision; the docs census and a source census hold every epoch-1 word left in `src/` outside migration and upgrade paths to a reasoned allowlist row, and no such file may spell an epoch-1 id.

35	- **The bundled `state.schema.json` describes the generation document,** with one object of rows per collection, instead of the v1 State model; `plan-view.schema.json` and the plan view renderer are deleted, as are the unraised error codes `WAVE_DEPS_NOT_SATISFIED`, `PHASE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ITER_NOT_ACTIVE` and `WAVE_OUT_OF_ORDER_REJECTED`.

36	- **The commit gates keep only the native grammar.** The wave, bare phase and `Eawf-Wave` commit forms, the open-phase rule and the release annotation check are gone, with the `wave-trailer-guard`, `spec-paths` and `eawf016-title-clarity` hooks; history written in the old subject forms still passes `--check-history`.

37	- **Imported backlog rows can leave the backlog.** `eawf task drop` on an epoch-1 key the cutover imported files the row as DROPPED without rewriting the sealed snapshot; a second drop is refused with `legacy_edge_refused`.

38	- **A committed ledger append advances the committed sequence,** so callers reading it are no longer refused with a revision conflict, and `eawf publish` stages a first, unstaged path whole instead of leaving `state.json` dirty and refusing the next publish with `publish_dirty_tree`.
39	- **Claude usage is folded at each message's latest reading,** so output tokens are no longer undercounted for the budget meter and the scorecard.
40	- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

41	- **Render lock files are bounded.** Render targets map onto 256 fixed stripe lock files instead of one file per target path, and the daemon test harnesses remove each whole runtime directory on teardown.
42	- **`eawf doctor` warns instead of crashing on a malformed config layer;** the local-size check degrades to a warning naming the merge failure.

43	- **Repository settings load in current Claude Code.** The managed metadata block in `.claude/settings.json` now names its hook list `hook_scripts`: Claude Code 2.1.310 refused the whole file while that block carried its own `hooks` key, which dropped every eawf hook, the status line and the env settings of a repository install. `eawf plugin update claude` rewrites an rc2 install.

44	- **A reopened review cannot reuse an earlier seal.** `eawf milestone open-review` now requires the acceptance bundle revision after the newest filed bundle, or revision 1 when none is filed. Before, a review reopened and opened again on revision 1 let an approval sealed in the earlier review accept the Milestone. The console no longer suggests `eawf milestone accept`, or an earlier review's waiting question, for a reopened Milestone.

45	- **A freshly initialised tree has its project row,** so memory, MCP, dispatch-control and `record append` writes work right after `eawf init`; `eawf why` explains decisions imported from the old model, and init reports the generation document as its state path.

46	- **`eawf plugin doctor claude` flags an rc2 install** whose settings Claude Code refuses or whose `Stop` hook no longer runs, and reports hooks loaded twice beside the marketplace plugin, each with its fix; agent pages no longer carry a `memory` key Claude Code rejects.

47	- **Safer maintenance.** Cancelling a Milestone asks a running Task's live Run to cancel, `eawf milestone purge` refuses while another record names the purged work, a retried legacy `task drop` replays its receipt, and `eawf local gc` keeps an expired entry that holds an unexpired one.

48	- **Leaner Run receipts and honest totals.** A `repo_read` receipt is stored by digest instead of text, a repeat read matches only the same file and launch, dispatch scoring counts each API call once, and `eawf reflect` counts as unpriced only Runs that reported tokens without a cost.

49	- **Upgrades keep work moving.** A governor written before `cache_read_weight` keeps its digest, so a Run admitted under rc2 resumes, and a gate stored with a legacy cadence keeps its digest, so its receipts stay fresh.
50	- **The release re-typed-rule census counts only operator-typed prose,** not the prompts an orchestrating agent sends its subagents.

51	- **Server checkout and runtime paths no longer reach committed state.** The leak scan treats a path under `/srv`, a `/run/user/<uid>` runtime directory and a `pytest-of-<user>` temp root like a home directory, so captured Run output withholds the line, a state write carrying one is refused and `path-leak-lint` flags it; the epoch-1 cutover scan keeps its three home anchors.

55	- **Agent report bodies use native field names.** `wave_id`, `waves`, `phase_id` and `completed_wave_ids` are now `task_key`, `tasks`, `milestone_key` and `completed_task_keys`; a new body naming an old field is refused with `extra_forbidden`, while a stored row is upgraded once on read and never rewritten.

56	- **Audit and gate cadences name native scopes.** `every-wave` becomes `every-task`, `every-iter` becomes `every-batch` and `every-phase` becomes `every-milestone`; `ship` and `manual` stay. A stored gate row reads an old value as its native one, an authored profile check or audit document naming one is refused with the value to write, and the `eawf doctor --fix` config normalisation rewrites each layer once.

57	- **Rule and profile block ids are renamed** where they spelled an epoch-1 noun, among them `wave-verification-scope` to `task-verification-scope`, `repo.phase-equals-release` to `repo.milestone-equals-release` and `repo.large-phase-pr` to `repo.large-milestone-pr`; re-render with `eawf sync`, and re-render installed hooks with `eawf plugin update claude`.

58	- **Retired settings.** `planning.max_parallel_waves`, `verify.require_iter_audit_accepted`, `daemon.session_handle_ttl_seconds`, `dispatch.role_tier_token_cap` and `profiles.certified` have no reader left and are deprecated. `eawf doctor` names each one a layer still states; remove it with `eawf config unset <key>` (add `--scope local|global|workspace` for another layer) or `eawf doctor --fix`.

62	- **`eawf workspace rekey-repo` moves registry rows only;** it does not rewrite store rows whose URNs carry the old workspace key, and neither new workspace verb is served by a daemon remote procedure call (RPC) yet.

"""The append-only ledger: what a line is, and why one is never edited.
A ledger line is written once. It is never rewritten, reordered or
removed, because every derived index, every digest taken over the file
and every reader that remembers a byte offset assumes the prefix it
already read cannot change underneath it. A wrong line is corrected by
appending a line that names the digest of the line it supersedes, so the
correction and the thing it corrects are both still readable.
The guard is structural rather than advisory.
:func:`verify_append_only` refuses any content that is not an extension
of what the file already holds, which catches a rewrite, a reorder and a
removal with one check, and :func:`guarded_ledger_write` is the only
sanctioned way to replace a ledger's bytes wholesale. The one exception is
:func:`replace_unpublished_suffix`, which may change only lines written
after the file's last commit, so a leak is taken out before any clone
A ledger may be sealed once (:func:`seal_ledger_prefix`): a leading run of
its lines moves, byte for byte, into ``snapshots/<stem>.<sha256>.jsonl``
beside it, and the live file keeps only what follows. The ledger a reader
sees is the snapshot's bytes followed by the live file's, so sealing
changes no record, no order and no digest; it only stops every later
commit of the live file from re-storing the sealed bytes. The snapshot is
named by its own sha256, and a snapshot whose bytes no longer hash to
that name is refused rather than read.

"""The append-only ledger: what a line is, and why one is never edited.
A ledger line is written once. It is never rewritten, reordered or
removed, because every derived index, every digest taken over the file
and every reader that remembers a byte offset assumes the prefix it
already read cannot change underneath it. A wrong line is corrected by
appending a line that names the digest of the line it supersedes, so the
correction and the thing it corrects are both still readable.
The guard is structural rather than advisory.
:func:`verify_append_only` refuses any content that is not an extension
of what the file already holds, which catches a rewrite, a reorder and a
removal with one check, and :func:`guarded_ledger_write` is the only

- **The epoch-1 engine is removed from every live surface.** `eawf status` reads only the native generation and reports the primary Track, active Milestone, open Tasks and native decisions; the daemon no longer schedules its stale-wave and session time-to-live sweeps; the v1 state readers are ported to the generation or retired, among them the epoch-1 `why` targets and the v1-only doctor checks; and the close-gate and spec-jury chain and other code with no production caller is deleted, with lint

- **Retired verbs.** `eawf jury label` exits 2 with `LegacyOperationRemoved` naming `eawf batch label`, and `eawf jury` is an unknown command; `eawf impact` is retired; `eawf release pipeline` takes `--milestone` as its only, required subject, so `--phase` is a usage error, and the phase-release workflow is gone.

- **The Claude Code plugin hooks load and report on a native tree.** The hook manifest is written to `hooks/hooks.json`, where Claude Code reads it, the session-end hook subscribes to SessionEnd instead of Stop, which fires every turn, and the agent_end and agent-output hooks resolve role and scope from the native Run instead of v1 state.

- **The shipped rules, profiles, role pages, help topics and skill bodies teach the native model** of Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and PlanRevision; the docs census and a source census hold every epoch-1 word left in `src/` outside migration and upgrade paths to a reasoned allowlist row, and no such file may spell an epoch-1 id.

- **The bundled `state.schema.json` describes the generation document,** with one object of rows per collection, instead of the v1 State model; `plan-view.schema.json` and the plan view renderer are deleted, as are the unraised error codes `WAVE_DEPS_NOT_SATISFIED`, `PHASE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ITER_NOT_ACTIVE` and `WAVE_OUT_OF_ORDER_REJECTED`.

- **The commit gates keep only the native grammar.** The wave, bare phase and `Eawf-Wave` commit forms, the open-phase rule and the release annotation check are gone, with the `wave-trailer-guard`, `spec-paths` and `eawf016-title-clarity` hooks; history written in the old subject forms still passes `--check-history`.

- **Imported backlog rows can leave the backlog.** `eawf task drop` on an epoch-1 key the cutover imported files the row as DROPPED without rewriting the sealed snapshot; a second drop is refused with `legacy_edge_refused`.

- **A committed ledger append advances the committed sequence,** so callers reading it are no longer refused with a revision conflict, and `eawf publish` stages a first, unstaged path whole instead of leaving `state.json` dirty and refusing the next publish with `publish_dirty_tree`.
- **Claude usage is folded at each message's latest reading,** so output tokens are no longer undercounted for the budget meter and the scorecard.
- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

- **Render lock files are bounded.** Render targets map onto 256 fixed stripe lock files instead of one file per target path, and the daemon test harnesses remove each whole runtime directory on teardown.
- **`eawf doctor` warns instead of crashing on a malformed config layer;** the local-size check degrades to a warning naming the merge failure.

- **Repository settings load in current Claude Code.** The managed metadata block in `.claude/settings.json` now names its hook list `hook_scripts`: Claude Code 2.1.310 refused the whole file while that block carried its own `hooks` key, which dropped every eawf hook, the status line and the env settings of a repository install. `eawf plugin update claude` rewrites an rc2 install.

- **A reopened review cannot reuse an earlier seal.** `eawf milestone open-review` now requires the acceptance bundle revision after the newest filed bundle, or revision 1 when none is filed. Before, a review reopened and opened again on revision 1 let an approval sealed in the earlier review accept the Milestone. The console no longer suggests `eawf milestone accept`, or an earlier review's waiting question, for a reopened Milestone.

- **A freshly initialised tree has its project row,** so memory, MCP, dispatch-control and `record append` writes work right after `eawf init`; `eawf why` explains decisions imported from the old model, and init reports the generation document as its state path.

- **`eawf plugin doctor claude` flags an rc2 install** whose settings Claude Code refuses or whose `Stop` hook no longer runs, and reports hooks loaded twice beside the marketplace plugin, each with its fix; agent pages no longer carry a `memory` key Claude Code rejects.

- **Safer maintenance.** Cancelling a Milestone asks a running Task's live Run to cancel, `eawf milestone purge` refuses while another record names the purged work, a retried legacy `task drop` replays its receipt, and `eawf local gc` keeps an expired entry that holds an unexpired one.

- **Leaner Run receipts and honest totals.** A `repo_read` receipt is stored by digest instead of text, a repeat read matches only the same file and launch, dispatch scoring counts each API call once, and `eawf reflect` counts as unpriced only Runs that reported tokens without a cost.

- **Upgrades keep work moving.** A governor written before `cache_read_weight` keeps its digest, so a Run admitted under rc2 resumes, and a gate stored with a legacy cadence keeps its digest, so its receipts stay fresh.

- **Breaking: the epoch-1 drift reports are gone on every tree.** `eawf --json status` no longer carries the `drift` key or the per-wave `commit` field of its active waves, and `eawf doctor` no longer reports the `git_state_drift` or `iter_audit_links` rows, publishes `git_state_drift_detected` or offers the `commits.repin` and `audits.acknowledge-legacy` repairs. A script that reads any of them must stop.
- **`eawf status` exits 1 on a torn or invalid native decision ledger,** and the daemon boot no longer marks leftover sessions stale; close them with `eawf session close`.

- **Hook wrappers fall back to the project environment when eawf is off PATH.** They run `uv run --no-project eawf` only when `eawf` is on PATH and plain `uv run eawf` otherwise, so an eawf installed only as a project dependency no longer fails every hook closed. Re-render installed hooks with `eawf plugin update claude` and `eawf plugin update codex`; Codex can mark re-rendered hooks untrusted until you re-approve them, and `eawf plugin doctor codex` reports their trust state.

- An operator or an authorized agent may initiate this skill. Agent invocation never widens authority: it needs an enclosing Run, Task or Campaign scope whose compiled capsule already grants every read, write, RPC, budget and external effect below.

- Operator-only actions: `approve`, `apply`. An agent that reaches one files it with `eawf question open-decision` (`runtime.question.open_decision`), shows the bound question the answer carries, and stops; it never chooses the recommended option itself. In Codex the bound question is the answer's `numbered_prompt`, printed verbatim, and the operator's reply is relayed with `eawf question answer` (`runtime.question.answer_numbered`); the console answers the same record, and the first answer wins
- Effects: The roadmap read plus the PlanRevision submit, approve and apply verbs.

- Allowed RPCs: `projection.roadmap.read`, `planning.plan_revision.submit`, `planning.plan_revision.approve`, `planning.plan_revision.apply`, `runtime.question.answer_numbered`, `runtime.question.open_decision`. Any other RPC is denied before it reaches a handler.
- Canonical state changes only through those RPCs, and every mutating call carries `--expected-revision` and `--idempotency-key`.
- Executable grants come from the compiled capsule of the enclosing scope alone; nothing on this page adds or widens a tool, path, RPC, credential or external effect.

0. Triage uncertainty before you decompose anything. Enumerate the plan's load-bearing unknowns: the integration surfaces, external contracts, and design forks whose real behaviour the plan depends on. For each, name the MeasuredContract that answers it and cite it by ArtifactUrn, or record it as unmeasured. This is a required step, not planner judgment: every other step below derives from text already written, so a plan can be fully valid, fully traceable, and entirely speculative without it.
1. Read the Milestone contract: outcome, appetite, exclusions, and the acceptance journey. These are the promise. Everything you plan exists to satisfy a step of that journey.

2. Atomize the source. Every requirement in the brief or Milestone becomes a source atom with an anchored span. An atom either maps to a criterion or is dropped explicitly with a reason and a Decision reference. Silent loss is the defect this step exists to prevent.

3. Decompose into Delivery Batches and Tasks. One Batch per repository. Give each Task one role, non-overlapping ownership claims, explicit dependencies with the proof each requires, and at least one criterion.

4. Write criteria that can fail. Each carries a typed response clause: what is observed, on what subject, where the proof lives, and what value is expected. A criterion no gate can falsify is not a criterion. Each also carries its grounding - measured, assumed, or accepted-risk - and a measured criterion cites the contract it rests on by ArtifactUrn rather than describing it.

5. Check your own plan against the deterministic lenses before submitting: every atom mapped or dropped, every outcome reachable, no dependency cycle, no concurrent write overlap, every criterion covered by a gate.
6. Submit. The daemon validates and either rejects with findings or marks the revision valid. Approval and apply are separate operator acts.
The obligations the effective rule graph holds for activities `plan` and roles `planner`. They bind what you do; they grant no capability.

- must: **Give every activity a non-empty rule set.** Keep every activity governed by at least one rule; an activity whose effective rule set is empty is a defect, never a statement that no rules apply.

- must: **Scope conduct rules to the closed activity set.** Scope an activity-bound rule only to research, plan, design, implement, test, review, integrate, commit, release, deploy or operate; a rule scoped to any other activity is refused with the offending value named.

- must: **Block on a question only when proceeding is unsafe.** Raise a blocking question only when proceeding under any available assumption would be unsafe or would make the work useless if wrong; resolve every other uncertainty by assumption plus disclosure.

- must: **Dispatch independent units of work together.** Dispatch independent units of work together rather than in sequence, where neither consumes the other's output; a sequential dispatch of independent units is a recorded miss.

- must: **Evaluate the practice set at each decision point.** Evaluate the applicable practice set at each decision point rather than recalling it: at least before dispatching work, before presenting a choice to the operator and before emitting a terminal report.

- must: **Expand every abbreviation on first use.** Expand every abbreviation, internal code and lifecycle identifier on first use in an operator-facing surface; write for a competent newcomer, not for the author of the state.

- must: **State the concern once and finish the task.** When a task looks ill-specified, state the concern once, record the assumption you proceed under and complete the work; do not halt and do not silently substitute your own reading.
- must: **Finish independent work before raising a question.** Before raising a question, complete all work that does not depend on its answer, and raise it only where the dependent work begins.

- must: **Recommend the option best for the long term.** Mark the option best for the long term as recommended and state why; where the repository configures a value the choice would override, show the configured value beside the recommendation.

- must: **Decide instead of asking when every option is the same work.** Do not ask a question with no consequence: where every option leads to the same work, select one, state the selection and proceed.
- must: **Retrieve the current practice set in one step.** Retrieve the practice set for the current activity with one query at each decision point instead of remembering which practices apply.

- must: **Record a scope delta before widening the work.** Record a typed scope delta against the task before any widening work begins; an unrecorded widening fails review even when the added work is correct.

- must: **Surface a decision as a typed choice with named options.** Surface a decision as a typed choice with named options, never as free text, and give each option a plain-prose description of what happens if it is selected.

- must: **Map every brief deliverable to a criterion or a deferral.** Map every enumerated brief deliverable to a criterion or to an explicit deferral row with its reason and target; while any span stays unmapped, halt planning with verdict=blocked naming the span.

- must: **Mark a criterion deterministic wherever a falsifier exists.** Set evidence_kind to deterministic wherever a falsifier exists, and to attested only for a claim that is genuinely judgment-bound.

- must: **Pin stable contracts verbatim in criterion text.** Pin stable contracts verbatim in the criterion text, such as digit and key maps, enum values, schemas and API shapes; a criterion that names only a chassis is a thinning defect.

- must: **Emit only typed criteria with a proof locus and a gate.** Give every emitted Task typed criteria (kind other than legacy), each with a response clause naming the observed verb, the object and a file:line proof locus, and at least one gate, usually a targeted pytest command, with policy=block and required=true.

- should: **Show a concrete rendering when options differ in structure.** Where options differ structurally, give each a concrete rendering of its outcome, such as a layout, a diagram or a worked example, rather than a description of the difference.

- An acceptance-mapped criterion still at assumed blocks APPROVE. There are exactly two exits: cite a SpikeReport or MeasuredContract to reach measured, or record an operator waiver Decision to reach accepted-risk, which carries a resolvable DecisionUrn. Learn the gate here rather than from a rejection.
- You cannot assign an observed head, a validation result, an approval, or any lifecycle state.
- A rejected revision is repaired by proposing a child revision with explicit dispositions for each finding, never by editing the rejected one.
- Do not plan work the exclusions forbid. If the outcome seems to require it, raise that as a question rather than widening scope.
- Stopping is a valid outcome, not a failure: when the answer needs an operator or a precondition fails, return `blocked` with the reason rather than guessing.

One strict PlanRevision proposal, plus the atom-to-criterion coverage table, every atom you dropped with its reason, and the uncertainty register from step 0 with each unknown either resolved to a cited contract or named as unmeasured.

Eä names every durable workflow object with a URN, a persistent and location-independent name. A URN survives file moves and resolves across workspace and repository boundaries. Two forms are in use: the qualified `eawf://` URN addresses the lifecycle entities (Track, Milestone, Batch, Task, Run and their neighbours), and the `urn:eawf:v1:` URN addresses store records, artifacts, blobs and version-control objects. The full reference lives in `docs/reference/urn-namespace.md`.

- The repository slot is never omitted. A workspace- or project-level entity (a release, a claim) takes the reserved `_`; a repository-level entity (a Milestone, a Batch, a Task, a Run) names its repository.
- The entity kind is one of the `EntityKind` values in `src/eawf/kernel/identity/keys.py`, and it must agree with the kind of reference that carries the URN.
- The entity key follows its kind's grammar: a Task is `<PROJECT>-####`, a Run `RUN-` with eight digits, a Milestone `MLS-####`, a Batch `BAT-####`, a Track `TRK-<symbol>`, a release `REL-<version>`.
- The only fragment is `#rung-<n>` on a claim URN, selecting evidence rung 1 to 4.
- A re-keyed tree spells the same address with one key in every container slot: `eawf://<project-key>/<entity-kind>/<entity-key>`.
- The namespace is `eawf` and the version `v1` immediately follows it.
- The kind is lowercase ASCII; `URN_KINDS` in `src/eawf/kernel/state/urn.py` is the catalog.
- The owner is the uppercase project code.
- The assigned name (everything before `?=` or `#`) is the identity; the query and fragment are view and selection hints and are ignored for equality.

9:This is the third release candidate of v0.7.0. The epoch-1 engine is gone from every live surface: `eawf init` bears a tree native at epoch 2, and no verb, daemon loop, rule, agent page or test reads or teaches the phase, iter and wave model any more, leaving only the migration and upgrade path to read v1 state. The Claude Code hooks load and report on a native tree; operators can edit, cancel, purge and rename Milestones and Tracks, list and show every entity, title a Task, join a workspace a

18:- **Join a workspace after init.** `eawf init --workspace <KEY>` joins a registered workspace at birth and refuses an unregistered key before the tree is born; `eawf workspace rekey-repo --to <KEY>` moves a repository out of its own single-member workspace into another, and `eawf workspace remove <KEY>` drops a workspace with exactly one member.
47:- **The claude-code canary is contained in the Linux bubblewrap jail:** storage masks are remounted read-only after the binds, so the write-ahead log and the workspace parent refuse writes.

68:- **Retired settings.** `planning.max_parallel_waves`, `verify.require_iter_audit_accepted`, `daemon.session_handle_ttl_seconds`, `dispatch.role_tier_token_cap` and `profiles.certified` have no reader left and are deprecated. `eawf doctor` names each one a layer still states; remove it with `eawf config unset <key>` (add `--scope local|global|workspace` for another layer) or `eawf doctor --fix`.

73:- **`eawf workspace rekey-repo` moves registry rows only;** it does not rewrite store rows whose URNs carry the old workspace key, and neither new workspace verb is served by a daemon remote procedure call (RPC) yet.

74:- **Not in this release:** a multi-project aggregate console route, `eawf reflect` cohorts, estimate-versus-actual variance and workspace-wide reflect scopes are planned for 0.7.1, and prose is not yet rewritten to STE; only the advisory lint ships.

83:- **Worker tools.** A Run's worker holds only its MCP (Model Context Protocol) server's granted tools: `workspace_apply_patch` (whole-file writes inside the Task's write set), `repo_read` and `repo_search` (bounded text from the leased workspace, refusing `.ea`, `.git` and link escapes) and `submit_report`, which takes report content only (verdict, summary, criterion outcomes and a body) while the daemon fills the schema and contract digest from the Run's capsule.

89:- **A Milestone closes before its pull request.** `eawf release show` reports `remote_facts`: merged (the source commit is an ancestor of origin's default branch) and tagged (`v<version>` on origin), derived from the remote at read time and never written to state, so acceptance waits on neither a merge nor a tag. A machine-local cache under `.ea/local` answers only when origin does not; `eawf release show` honours `--workspace`.
